# lcd.drawBitmap

<div class="api-badges"><span class="api-badge api-badge--since">since 1.1.0</span></div>

Draw a bitmap.

```lua
lcd.drawBitmap(x, y, bitmap[, w[, h]])
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | number | yes | X coordinate |
| `y` | number | yes | Y coordinate |
| `bitmap` | [Bitmap](../objects/Bitmap/index.md) | yes | bitmap |
| `w` | number | optional (default `0`) | the width of the bitmap displayed |
| `h` | number | optional (default `0`) | the height of the bitmap display |

## Returns

Nothing.

## Examples

```lua
local LOGO = lcd.loadBitmap("gfx/logo.png")

local function paint(widget)
  local w, h = lcd.getWindowSize()
  if not LOGO then return end
  lcd.drawBitmap(0, 0, LOGO)                 -- natural size
  lcd.drawBitmap(w - 64, 0, LOGO, 64, 64)    -- scaled into a 64x64 box
end
```

Scaling at draw time is convenient, but an image that is always shown small should be stored small: the decoded size is what costs RAM.
